featured_reviews.name: Hasting Square
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience with the ENAM India Vision Portfolio over approximately two and a half years was ultimately disappointing from both a performance and professional management perspective.

At the outset, the portfolio was presented as a high-conviction investment strategy with long-term wealth creation potential. However, during my investment period, the portfolio significantly underperformed not only major benchmark indices but even conservative fixed deposit (FD) rates. After accounting for inflation and opportunity cost, the real return was effectively negligible. In practical terms, I felt as though I had provided capital for an extended period without receiving an adequate return for the risk undertaken.

One of my primary concerns was the lack of analytical transparency behind investment decisions. Conviction investing and qualitative judgment certainly have a place in portfolio management, but they should be supported by clear financial reasoning and valuation frameworks. Throughout my engagement, I found it difficult to obtain meaningful explanations regarding projected earnings, expected returns, valuation assumptions, downside analysis, or the mathematical rationale supporting particular investments. Discussions often relied more on broad narratives and “long-term conviction” rather than disciplined portfolio analytics.

The communication and client servicing were also below expectations for a professional portfolio management service. While the team was generally courteous and pleasant in conversations, the follow-through lacked consistency. Periodic review meetings were promised but often delayed or absent for months at a time. Even during meetings, the explanations frequently centered around the idea that the portfolio was “settling” rather than providing measurable benchmarks, accountability metrics, or a detailed strategy review.

Another issue appeared to be operational capacity. The organization seemed significantly understaffed relative to the level of service expected from a professional investment management platform. This was reflected not only in communication delays but also in the quality and frequency of disclosures, reporting clarity, and portfolio transparency.

To be fair, I was able to exit the investment with approximately enough gains to cover transactional and administrative costs, so I did not incur a major nominal loss. However, considering inflation, time value of money, and the performance available through passive index investing, the outcome was materially disappointing.

Ironically, my subsequent experience using AI-assisted portfolio analysis and systematic investment frameworks has been considerably more effective.
